healthcareSystem: Mixed public/private. Public healthcare (State hospitals) is available but often overcrowded with long wait times. Private healthcare (medical schemes) offers excellent care comparable to first-world standards.
qualityNotes: Private healthcare in South Africa is excellent and world-class, with JCI-accredited hospitals in major cities. State hospitals are basic and overcrowded. Medical staff are well-trained. Pharmacies (Clicks, Dis-Chem, independent) are widely available. Private ambulance services (ER24, Netcare 911) are excellent but expensive.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 8am-9pm; some 24-hour pharmacies in major cities; chains include Clicks, Dis-Chem Pharmacies, and independent pharmacies
pharmacyTips: Many common medications available OTC. Pharmacists are helpful and knowledgeable. Bring a list of medications with generic names. Some medications may not be available — bring your supply. Malaria prophylaxis is important for certain regions.
prescriptionRules: A prescription is required for prescription medications. Foreign prescriptions are not accepted — you need a South African prescription. Carry all medications in original packaging with a doctor's note.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD stimulant medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Stimulants are Schedule 6 controlled substances. Bring original prescription, doctor's letter, and only the amount needed. You may need a permit from the South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) for certain quantities.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is a Schedule 5/6 substance. Some products available with prescription. Many codeine products require a prescription. Carry alternatives if possible.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (diazepam, alprazolam, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Benzodiazepines are controlled. Carry a doctor's letter explaining medical necessity.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis (medical or recreational)
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in South Africa despite some decriminalization for personal use. Do not bring any cannabis products.

restrictedMeds.name: Methylphenidate (Ritalin/Concerta)
restrictedMeds.note: Schedule 6 controlled. Bring documentation and SAHPRA permit if carrying significant quantities.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry original prescriptions and a note explaining medical necessity. Check SAHPRA requirements if carrying Schedule 5-6 substances for extended stays.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Required for visa applications but not for entry. Strongly recommended for all travelers. Medical care without insurance in private hospitals can be expensive ($1,000-5,000+/day).
travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance is strongly recommended. State hospitals are free but overcrowded. Private healthcare is excellent but expensive without insurance. Medical evacuation coverage is essential, especially for safari ( Kruger) and remote areas. Crime-related injuries are also a risk — ensure coverage includes trauma and emergency medical services.

recommended: Typhoid (for extended stays or rural travel)
Yellow Fever (required if arriving from a yellow fever endemic country)
Rabies (for animal exposure, especially dogs and wildlife)
Malaria prophylaxis (for travel to Kruger National Park and surrounding areas, and KwaZulu-Natal lowlands during summer months)
vaccinations.notes: No required vaccinations for most travelers unless arriving from a yellow fever endemic country. Malaria is a risk in Kruger National Park and some coastal areas — take prophylaxis (Larium/mefloquine, Malarone, or doxycycline). Rabies is present in some areas — avoid contact with dogs and wild animals.

waterNotes: Tap water is generally safe to drink in major cities (Johannesburg, Cape Town, Durban). In rural areas, use bottled or filtered water as a precaution. In Cape Town, tap water is excellent. Bottled water is widely available everywhere.
foodSafetyTips: South Africa has good food safety standards in restaurants, hotels, and supermarkets. In Cape Town and major cities, restaurants maintain excellent hygiene. Be cautious with street food in informal areas. South African wine country and safari lodges maintain high standards. Avoid meat from informal vendors.
medicalTourismNote: South Africa is a well-established medical tourism destination, particularly for cosmetic surgery, cardiac surgery, and fertility treatments. Costs are 50-80% lower than in the US and UK. Cape Town and Johannesburg have world-class JCI-accredited private hospitals. Popular for tummy tucks, breast augmentations, and cardiac procedures.

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care available, especially in major cities.
dentalCare.costRange: ZAR 500-1,200 ($28-67) for consultation; ZAR 800-2,500 ($45-140) for fillings
dentalCare.notes: Private dental care is high quality in Cape Town and Johannesburg. Affordable by international standards.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Private hospital emergency departments handle dental emergencies. Dischem and Clicks pharmacies can provide pain relief.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Widely available. English is commonly spoken.
mentalHealth.notes: South Africa has good mental health services in urban areas. SADAG provides comprehensive support. Private therapy: ZAR 600-1,500 per session.

accessibilityInfo.overview: South Africa has legal accessibility requirements but enforcement varies. Major cities have improving infrastructure.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Gautrain in Johannesburg is accessible. MyCiti buses in Cape Town are accessible. Taxis and Uber widely available.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Table Mountain cable car is wheelchair accessible. Kruger National Park has some accessible safari vehicles and lodges. V&A Waterfront in Cape Town is fully accessible.

covidStatus.notes: Malaria prophylaxis recommended for Kruger Park area. Sun exposure is a significant concern.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private hospitals require payment or insurance guarantee. Netcare and Mediclinic have insurance departments. Public hospitals treat emergencies at lower cost. Keep all receipts and medical reports.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private or international facilities. Public-system rates can be much lower (or free for residents). Actual costs vary by city, facility, and exchange rate.

medicalEvacuation.primaryDestination: Local treatment is excellent in major cities
medicalEvacuation.note: Local hospitals handle the vast majority of cases — air evacuation is rarely needed for tourists. If a condition exceeds local capacity: South African private hospital groups (Mediclinic, Netcare, Life Healthcare) operate world-class facilities in Cape Town, Johannesburg, and Durban.
